# Multi-Turn Conversation Guide
LLMs have **no memory of their own** — a model doesn't remember what you said a moment ago.
A "multi-turn conversation" really just means **sending the full conversation history with every request**.
...
## Core principle: maintain history yourself
One sentence covers it: **the model is stateless; you (the client) maintain the history and resend all of it every turn.**
...
Each new turn, **append** the previous user message and model reply to the end of the history array, then send the whole thing.
...
## OpenAI compatible mode (works across models)
The most universal approach, endpoint `/v1/chat/completions`.
History lives in the `messages` array, each entry carrying a `role` (`system` / `user` / `assistant`).
...
### Handling history for reasoning models
**Keep only `content` in the history — do not pass `reasoning_content` back.** The thinking is just an intermediate product of the current turn; passing it back wastes tokens and violates upstream rules (DeepSeek's direct API even returns a 400 for it).
...
## OpenAI native format (Responses API)
Endpoint `/v1/responses`.
For multi-turn, **pass the full history as the `input` array** (each entry with `role` / `content`) — the same self-managed approach as compatible mode:
...
## Gemini native format
Endpoint `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`.
History lives in the `contents` array.
Note the **roles are `user` / `model`** (not `assistant`), and each entry's content goes in `parts`.
